T or I: A2 [ T or I ] to make something by putting bricks or other materials together

NONE: › the size and shape of a person's body
身材，體形

T: › [ T ] to create and develop something over a long period of time

example: They're building new houses by the river.
他們正在河邊建新房子。
The birds built their nest in the tree.
鳥兒們在樹上築巢。
These old houses are built (= made) of stone.
這些老房子是用石頭砌的。

承包商開始在離城鎮不遠的廢棄土地上建房。

我們想為孩子創造更美好的未來。
She was of slim build with short, dark hair.
她身材苗條，一頭黑色的短髮。

NONE: C1 to increase or become larger or stronger, or to cause someone or something to do this
增強，加強；增大

example: Tension is building up between the two communities.
兩個社區之間的關係日趨緊張。
They gave him soup to build up his strength.
他們給他喝湯以增強體質。
It took her ten years to build up her publishing business.
她花了十年時間將她的出版事業發展壯大。

NONE: › to base something on an idea or principle
以…為基礎

example: The independence movement sought to unify the country with a national identity built around a common language.
獨立運動謀求以建立在共同語言基礎上的民族認同感來統一國家。

NONE: › to improve relationships between people who are very different or do not like each other
改善或加強不同（或敵對）人士或組群間的關係

example: A local charity is working to build bridges between different ethnic groups in the area.
一家地方慈善機構正努力在這個地區不同的族群間架設友誼的橋樑。

NONE: › to use a success or achievement as a base from which to achieve more success
基於，依賴，以…為基礎

example: We must build on our reputation to expand the business.
我們必須依靠信譽來擴展業務。
A good relationship is built on trust.
良好的關係建立在信任的基礎上。

NONE: › to include something as part of a plan, system, or agreement
（使）包括；使成為（計劃、系統或協議的）組成部分

example: When drawing up a contract it is vital to build in safety measures.
草擬合同時，將安全措施包括在內很重要。
figurative Inequalities are often built into (= cannot be separated from) society.
社會中往往會存在不平等現象。

NONE: › to praise something or someone in a way that will influence people's opinions; to make a person feel more confident
讚揚；吹捧

example: A good teacher builds you up.
一個好老師會幫助增強你的信心。
For weeks the media has been building up the national basketball team.
媒體幾週來一直在吹捧國家籃球隊。

C usually singular: › an increase, especially one that is gradual
› a situation in which someone or something is praised, advertised, or talked about on the internet, in newspapers, etc.
› UK the period of preparation before something happens

example: The build-up of troops in the region makes war seem more likely.
在這一地區集結軍隊加大了戰爭爆發的可能性。
The group got a big build-up before their tour, being touted by many as the next Beatles.
在巡迴演出前對該樂隊進行了大規模的宣傳，許多人將其吹捧為新一代披頭四樂隊。
There was a lot of excitement in the build-up to the Olympics.
奧運的前期準備工作中有許多讓人興奮的事。

NONE: B1 a person whose job it is to make buildings

U: A2 [ U ] the process or business of making structures such as houses or factories

一度空蕩蕩的地方現在布滿了建築物。

› the basic things that are put together to make something exist

example: Science and the arts are the building blocks of a good education.

NONE: › a piece of land on which a house or other building is being built
